decision_conditions: The development to which this permission relates must be commenced not later than three years from the date of this permission.
Reason: To comply with the requirements of Section 91 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990 (as amended by Section 51 of the Planning and Compulsory Purchase Act 2004).
The development hereby approved shall not be carried out otherwise than in complete accordance with the following approved plans:

Prior to the commencement of the development hereby approved (including demolition and site clearance works), a Construction Logistics Plan (CLP) and a Construction and Environmental Management Plan (CEMP), shall be submitted to, and approved in writing by, the Local Planning Authority, to minimise impacts to the local highway network and to control noise, vibration and air pollutants generated as a result of the construction process. These documents shall be prepared in accordance with the most recently published version of the London Freight Plan, 'The control of dust and emissions from construction and demolition' Supplementary Planning Guidance, BRE Pollution Control Guides 'Controlling particles and noise pollution from construction sites' and 'Controlling particles, vapour and noise pollution from construction sites', and the IAQM's 'Guidance on the assessment of dust from demolition and construction'.

Prior to the commencement of the development hereby approved (including demolition and site clearance works), the following information shall be submitted to, and approved in writing by, the local planning authority:

a)	A Phase I (Desktop Study) Report documenting the history of the site, its surrounding area and the likelihood of contaminant/s, their type and extent incorporating a Site Conceptual Model, based on the Phase 1 Report (RSK Geosciences, dated October 2025).

b)	A Phase II (Site Investigation) Report if the Phase I Report confirms the possibility of a significant risk to any sensitive receptors.  This is an intrusive site investigation including factors such as chemical testing, quantitative risk assessment and a description of the sites ground conditions.  An updated Site Conceptual Model should be included showing all the potential pollutant linkages and an assessment of risk to identified receptors.

Prior to the commencement of the development hereby approved (excluding demolition and site clearance works), a revised Energy Strategy shall be submitted to, and approved in writing by, the Local Planning Authority.
The Revised Energy Strategy shall:

-	Demonstrate compliance with the Energy Hierarchy and achieve total regulated CO2 savings of at least 39.5% compared to Part L of the 2021 Building Regulations, achieving at least 26.7% of these savings through 'Be Lean' energy efficiency measures and at least 12.8% of these savings through 'Be Green' renewable technologies.

-	Provide further details on the use of individual systems for heating and cooling, including information relating to whether communal heating systems were explored and an explanation of why a communal system would not be more appropriate in reducing carbon emissions.

Prior to the commencement of the development hereby approved (excluding demolition and site clearance works), a revised Overheating Assessment shall be submitted to, and approved in writing by, the Local Planning Authority.
The Revised Overheating Assessment shall include:
-	A natural ventilation scenario (with windows open) (DSY1), with robust justification for any failures when testing units or communal areas against the baseline and updated g-value scenarios.
-	Annotated plans showing which habitable rooms or communal areas will be affected by noise constraints.

-	Measures to ensure that the proposed mechanical ventilation system provides an acceptable form of temperature control, including modelling of the DSY1 2020s weather file demonstrating where the rooms or communal areas that are constrained by noise will overheat when the windows are closed, and details of the appropriate overheating and/or noise mitigation measures in line with the Cooling Hierarchy and the Acoustics Vent

No Piling shall take place until a Piling Method Statement, detailing the depth and type of piing to be undertaken and the methodology by which piling will be carried out, including measures to prevent and minimise the potential for damage to subsurface sewerage infrastructure, and the programme for works, has been submitted to, and approved in writing by, the local planning authority in consultation with Thames Water.
Any piling must be undertaken in accordance with the terms of the approved piling method statement.
Reason: To protect underground sewerage utility infrastructure in accordance with Policy SI 17 of the London Plan (2021).

Prior to above ground works for the development hereby approved (excluding demolition and site clearance works), a combined Noise Mitigation Scheme and Ventilation/Overheating Strategy shall be submitted to, and approved in writing by, the Local Planning Authority.
The combined Noise Mitigation Scheme and Ventilation/Overheating Strategy shall include:

·	A full facade and glazing specification, demonstrating compliance with the internal ambient noise criteria set out in BS 8233:2014 for all habitable rooms, including explicit assessment of night-time LAFmax events arising from rail movements.
·	Acoustic performance data for all ventilation and cooling systems, confirming that required internal noise levels can be achieved with windows closed.
·	Evidence that the proposed overheating strategy is compliant with TM59, and that the required cooling and ventilation rates can be achieved without reliance on openable windows.
·	Details of any associated mechanical plant (including intake/ex

Prior to any above ground works (excluding demolition and site clearance works), a Biodiversity Enhancement Strategy for protected, priority and threatened species, and which shall have been prepared by a suitably qualified ecologist, shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority.
The content of the Biodiversity Enhancement Strategy shall include the following:
(a)	Purpose and conservation objectives for the proposed enhancement measures;
(b)	detailed designs or product descriptions to achieve stated objectives;
(c)	locations of proposed enhancement measures by appropriate maps and plans (where relevant);
(d)	persons responsible for implementing the enhancement measures; and
(e)	details of initial aftercare and long-term maintenance (where relevant).
The works shall be implemented in accordance with the approved details and shall be retained in that manner thereafter.
Reason: To enhance protected, priority and threatened species and allow the Local P

Prior to above ground works (excluding demolition and site clearance works), a detailed scheme of internal sound insulation, which shall also protect the proposed residential units from noise from the commercial uses, shall be submitted to, and approved in writing by, the local planning authority. Any works which form part of the scheme shall be completed before any of the approved dwellings are occupied, and maintained as such.

The ceiling/party floor insulation between the commercial and residential premises shall comply with the current Approved Document E of the Building Regulations 2003 (as amended), with reference to British Standard BS8233: 2014 - Sound insulation and noise reduction for buildings - Code of practice.
The scheme shall be designed to be 5dB better than that given in Approved Document E 2003 (as amended).
Reason: To protect residential amenity in accordance with Policy 34 of the Havering Local Plan (2021) and Policies D13 and D14 of the London Plan (2021

Prior to above ground works for the development hereby approved (excluding demolition and site clearance works), details and samples for all materials, including a schedule of their locations, shall be submitted to, and approved in writing by, the Local Planning Authority. Where relevant, the materials shall include walls, roofs, windows and doors, sills and lintels, balconies, balustrades, visible pipes, grids and louvers, outdoor pavements, stairs, gates, boundary walls and fences to be used on the external surfaces of the buildings and hard surfaced areas.
The development shall be constructed and retained for the lifetime of the development in full accordance with the approved details.
Reason: To ensure a high quality design in accordance with Policy 26 of the Havering Local Plan (2021).
Prior to above ground works (excluding demolition and site clearance works), a scheme of hard and soft landscaping shall be submitted to, and approved in writing by, the local planning authority.
The scheme shall include:
-	Planting plans;
-	Written specification of planting and cultivation works to be undertaken;
-	Schedule of plants, including species, plant sizes, proposed numbers and densities where appropriate;
-	Means of enclosure and boundary treatments;
-	Hard surfacing materials;
-	External lighting;
-	Living walls and roofs; and
-	Landscape maintenance.
Thereafter the scheme of landscaping shall be carried out prior to the first occupation of the development and maintained in full accordance with the approved details in perpetuity.
In addition, the proposal shall achieve an Urban Greening Factor (UGF) of at least 0.40.
Reason: To ensure that the proposed development will preserve and enhance the visual amenities of the locality and provide adequate facilities in complian

Prior to the first occupation of any part of the development hereby approved, a scheme setting out the Lighting Design Strategy for the site shall be submitted to, and approved in writing by, the Local Planning Authority. The scheme of lighting shall be prepared in accordance with Guidance Note 08/23 (Institute of Lighting Professionals), and shall demonstrate that the lighting scheme would not be harmful to wildlife.

The scheme of lighting shall identify those areas or features on site that are particularly sensitive for crepuscular and nocturnal species and that are likely to cause disturbance in or around their breeding sites and resting places or along important routes used to access key areas of their territory, for example, for foraging, and show how and where external lighting will be installed (through provision of appropriate lighting technical specifications) so that it can be clearly demonstrated that areas to be lit will not disturb or prevent sensitive species using their

Prior to the first occupation of the development hereby approved, a Noise Management Plan shall be submitted to, and approved in writing by, the Local Planning Authority. The Noise Management Plan shall set out how noise will be controlled within communal areas, how evening activities within the development will be managed, and arrangements for handling and responding to noise complaints.
Reason: to protect amenity in accordance with Policy 34 of the Havering Local Plan (2021).
Prior to the first occupation of any part of the development hereby approved, a Delivery and Servicing Plan shall be submitted to, and approved in writing by, the Local Planning Authority.
The Delivery and Servicing Plan shall include:
-	details of loading/unloading areas
-	booking systems
-	vehicle routing
-	frequency of deliveries
-	service hours
-	vehicle sizes
-	strategies for the consolidation of movements
-	the use of low-emission vehicles where possible
The development shall be operated in accordance with the approved details in perpetuity.
Reason: To ensure the development is managed effectively in accordance with Policy T7 of the London Plan (2021).

Prior to the first occupation of the development hereby approved, details of the public art provision, proposed for the facade facing South Street, shall be submitted to, and approved in writing by, the Local Planning Authority.
Reason: To ensure the development provides an acceptable level of public amenity in accordance with Policies D4 and D8 of the London Plan (2021).

Prior to the first occupation of the development hereby approved, a post-installation verification report shall be submitted to, and approved in writing by, the Local Planning Authority, which shall demonstrate that any mechanical plant associated with the development has been designed and installed to achieve a Rating Level at least 5 dB below background noise levels (calculated in accordance with BS 4142 at the nearest residential receptor).
Reason: To prevent noise nuisance arising from mechanical equipment, in accordance with Policy D14 of the London Plan (2021).

(A)	Prior to the first occupation of any part of the development hereby approved, and within 90 days of practical completion, a post-development survey of the culvert shall be submitted to, and approved in writing by, the Local Planning Authority. The survey shall demonstrate that the development has not caused any adverse impacts on the structural integrity of the culvert.

(B)	Any defects identified through the survey shall be made good at the applicant's expense and to the Local Planning Authority's satisfaction within a timeframe agreed with the Local Planning Authority.
Reason: To protect the integrity of the culverted watercourse beneath the site, in accordance with Policy SI 17 of the London Plan (2021).
The development hereby approved shall be implemented in accordance with the details contained within the 'Fire Statement (incl. Gateway One Form)' (October 2025).
Reason: To ensure compliance with Policy D12 of the London Plan (2021).

The development hereby approved shall achieve 'Secured by Design' accreditation awarded by the Havering Metropolitan Police Crime Prevention Design Adviser (CPDA) on behalf of the Association of Chief Police Officers (ACPO). No part of the development hereby approved shall be occupied until accreditation has been achieved.
Reason: To promote the use of security standards and crime prevention, in accordance Policy 26 of the Havering Local Plan (2021).
All ecological mitigation measures and works shall be carried out in accordance with the details contained in the submitted Ecological Assessment (Red Ecology, October 2025).

This shall include the appointment of an appropriately competent person (e.g. an ecological clerk of works) to provide on-site ecological expertise during construction. The appointed person shall undertake all activities, and works shall be carried out, in accordance with the approved details.

Reason: To conserve protected and Priority species and allow the Local Planning Authority to discharge its duties under the Conservation of Habitats and Species Regulations 2017 (as amended), the Wildlife & Countryside Act 1981 (as amended) and s40 of the NERC Act 2006 (as amended), and in accordance with Policy G6 of the London Plan (2021).

The generators installed for emergency standby life safety systems shall not be operated for routine testing for more than 18 hours per calendar year. Records concerning the routine testing shall be maintained at all times.
Reason: In order to prevent excessive emissions from the generator plant, and ensure the development remains air quality neutral, in accordance with Policy SI 1 of the London Plan (2021).
The development hereby approved shall comply with the details contained within the 'Shared Living Management Plan' (October 2025).
Reason: To ensure compliance with Policy H16 of the London Plan (2021).
The development hereby approved shall provide 28 of the shared-living units (10%) as wheelchair accessible units, with a minimum floorspace provision of 28 sqm.
In addition, the measures outlined in the 'Inclusive Design Statement' (October 2025), shall be implemented in full and maintained as such in perpetuity.
Reason: To ensure the development provides accommodation for all in accordance with Policy D5 of the London Plan (2021).
The development hereby approved shall comply with the details contained within the 'Operational Waste Management Plan' (October 2025).
Reason: To ensure that refuse and recycling is managed in an acceptable manner in accordance with Policy SI 7 of the London Plan (2021).

The development hereby approved shall provide one wheelchair accessible parking bay in accordance with Drawing No. 25002-CAL-100-100-DR-A-120100 (Rev. A) and this bay shall be retained in perpetuity. This bay shall be provided with an active electric vehicle charging point.
Reason: To ensure the development caters for those with mobility issues in accordance with Policy D5 of the London Plan (2021).

The development hereby approved shall provide at least 145 long-stay cycle spaces and at least 8 short-stay visitor cycle spaces, in accordance with Drawing No. 25002-CAL-100-100-DR-A-120100 (Rev. A) and these cycle spaces shall be retained in perpetuity.
Reason: To encourage cycling in accordance with Policy T5 of the London Plan (2021).
The development hereby approved shall be implemented in accordance with the details contained within the Flood Risk Assessment & Drainage Strategy (Rev. P03) (February 2026).
Reason: To ensure compliance with Policy SI 13 of the London Plan (2021).
The development hereby approved shall operate as co-living accommodation, providing 285 individual rooms for rent under a single management structure, falling within a Sui Generis Use Class.
Reason: To ensure the development complies with Policy H16 of the London Plan (2021).
description: Demolition of existing building to facilitate redevelopment comprising Shared Living Accommodation (Sui Generis) with ancillary facilities, which includes a commercial (Class E) unit on the ground floor, hard and soft landscaping, cycle parking, and other associated works.
